target_customer: Employers hiring STEM talent and STEM job seekers (free accounts for both)
problem: Employers and STEM graduates struggled to find each other on general job boards.
business_model: Job board with employer postings and recruiting tools (pricing not found)
product_category: STEM-specialized job board and recruiting marketplace

founders.name: Jorge Ortiz
founders.background_notes: Only founder named on the YC page; team size listed as 2.

competitors.name: Dice
competitors.what: Largest niche job board, focused on IT
competitors.traction_then: Launched in 1996, the dominant tech niche board

technical_complexity.rationale: A job board with profiles and matching was standard web development.

defensibility.rationale: Two-sided job boards need liquidity and established players already dominated; the STEM niche was easy to copy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents already served tech and general job seekers in 2008; no source shows the incumbents responding specifically to Joberator.

market_need_then: The online job search market was large and growing in 2008, with aggregators scaling quickly, but no evidence of unmet demand for a STEM-only board was found.

branding.domain_note: joberator.com is the directory site; it shows only a loading placeholder when fetched.

brand_strength.rationale: No press, community or visual identity material was found; name is easy to confuse with the later Joberate Inc. trademark.

outcome_analysis: Joberator was a two-person STEM job board in YC's Winter 2008 batch, now listed as inactive. The cause is not public: no shutdown notice, post-mortem or news coverage was found, and the website shows only a loading page. A niche board facing Dice, Indeed and Simply Hired plausibly lacked liquidity, but that is not established, so failure factors stay empty.
notes: CB Insights and Seedtable show a $20K seed from Y Combinator in January 2008 (aggregators only, not recorded as a round). CB Insights says headquarters St. Petersburg versus YC's Los Angeles listing. Parsers.vc marks the domain probably closed. Competitors are from 2008-era general job board coverage, not named rivals of Joberator. Founded year 2007 is an estimate from the batch date, not sourced. Completeness pass: the $20K January 2008 round from Y Combinator rests on a single database (CB Insights and Seedtable); it is the standard YC deal.
